historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of equity_5yr_cagr (5.5%) and a mid-cycle structural view, damped toward GDP-plus given the business is commodity-trading-margin, not a secular compounder
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue and EPS CAGRs are not meaningfully comparable across this window: FY2022 was a historic commodity-price boom (revenue $9.28bn) and FY2023/24 revenue fell sharply on both lower prices/volumes and the FY2024 UK Metal divestment (continuing-ops restatement), so the 3yr revenue CAGR is negative (-6.7%) purely from the high FY2022 base, not business decline. EPS CAGR is not computed (FY2024/FY2025 net income was negative). Equity CAGR (5.5% over 5yr, 0.6% over 3yr) is the most stable series and is used as the primary anchor, consistent with the method's preference for book-value growth in a cyclical/value context; even so, equity growth over FY22-25 is damped by buybacks and dividends funded from a peak-earnings year, so it likely understates normalized structural growth. Selected growth rate (4.0%) is a judgment blend, not a mechanical CAGR read.

scenario_narratives.base: Metal segment margins normalize mid-cycle as Chinese export oversupply gradually eases; SLS settles into a larger but calmer growth phase once the DDR4 spike fades per management's own guidance; SAR JV bolt-on M&A continues. EBITDA margin ramps 6.2% -> 6.8%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Non-ferrous/AI electrification tailwind persists, tariffs hold NAM/SAR margins up, ANZ recovers faster on new EAF capacity, and SLS avoids the feared FY27 air-pocket while GPU repurposing succeeds early. EBITDA margin ramps to 8.7%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY27 SLS guidance cut is the start of a full DDR4 unwind, Chinese export oversupply persists or worsens, and GPU repurposing stalls. EBITDA margin stays near the FY2025 trough, 4.3-5.0%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sims is valued on a mid-cycle, component-built owner-FCF DCF: FY0 revenue is anchored to the actual FY2026 outcome (A$8,007.5m, confirmed qualitatively via the 19-Sep-2026 results release since the annual filing is not yet extracted), but the EBITDA margin used to build forward cash flows is a normalized mid-cycle level (6.2% ramping to 6.8%), not the FY2026 underlying margin of ~9.1% that was substantially inflated by an acknowledged-transient DDR4 memory pricing spike, nor the FY2025 trough of 4.3%. This follows the house cyclical-adaptation rule: never extrapolate a peak or trough year as if it were the steady state. Leases are treated as debt (treatment A): lease principal is not deducted from flows, and lease liabilities (A$312.2m) are added to net debt (A$306.8m ex-lease) once in the equity bridge, matching the company's own net-debt and 'total capital' definitions. SA Recycling's equity-accounted JV profit is not separately adjusted because the FCF base is built from OCF (which already reflects actual cash SAR dividends, not accrual profit share) -- a simplification flagged rather than silently assumed. A 10-year horizon is used because the base-case margin is still ramping toward its mature level in year 5.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2026 annual report is not yet published/extracted -- the exact FY2026 year-end balance sheet (net debt, lease liabilities, diluted share count) is not independently verified; this DCF uses the latest verified filing (H1 FY2026, 31-Dec-2025) as the balance-sheet anchor and should be refreshed once the FY2026 annual is available

SLS/DDR4 earnings quality: FY2026's outperformance rests substantially on a >1000% YoY DDR4 price spike management itself guides to soften materially in H1 FY27 -- if the base case's mid-cycle margin assumption (6.2-6.8%) still proves too optimistic relative to a sharper unwind, bear-case risk is understated
Chinese steel export oversupply is an unresolved, open-ended structural headwind for ANZ and export-exposed NAM/SAR volumes with no management-guided resolution timeline

Only 50% economic ownership of SA Recycling limits consolidated capital-allocation control over roughly half the North American metals earnings base, and the equity-accounted-profit-vs-cash-dividend gap is a modelling simplification rather than a fully itemized adjustment

GPU repurposing, the next SLS growth leg beyond DDR4 memory, is unproven and early-stage with certification complexity management itself describes as an order of magnitude harder than memory -- bull case assumes early success that is not yet demonstrated

data_sources.qualitative: SGM.AX_Analysis.json, including the 19-Sep-2026 FY2026 full-year results release (revenue, underlying EBIT/NPAT, H1 FY27 SLS guidance) not yet reflected in the Metrics CSV

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual cash flow statement 'Share-based payments expense, net of tax' A$16.5m (H1 FY2026 A$6.6m annualizes to ~A$13.2m, declining trend); no separate equity-award-tax withholding line disclosed, so the cash-flow add-back is used as the full SBC charge
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (H1 FY2026, latest verified filing; FY2026 30-June-2026 balance sheet not yet extracted from an annual filing -- only qualitative P&L figures for FY2026 are available in the Analysis JSON)
inputs.share_count_date: 2025-12-31 (H1 FY2026 diluted weighted-average shares, 192.733m; FY2025 annual diluted was 195.325m -- buybacks/vesting have trimmed the count)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-denominated flows and AUD quote. AU 10yr risk-free ~4.3%, ERP ~5.5%, beta ~1.2 for a cyclical metal-recycling/trading-margin business gives cost of equity ~10.9%; blended down for ~15-20% of capital at low-cost secured/unsecured AUD/USD debt to a WACC of 9.5%, in line with the house range used for other AU cyclical industrials (BSL.AX, BAP.AX) in this folder.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A (leases as debt). Company's own 'Net debt' KPI (H1 FY26: A$306.8m) explicitly EXCLUDES lease liabilities (H1 FY26: A$312.2m, disclosed as a separate line) -- Total borrowings A$412.9m minus cash A$106.1m = net debt A$306.8m ties exactly. Lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows (it is not embedded in reported OCF; AASB16 lease principal repayments sit in financing activities). Lease liabilities are instead added to the net-debt bridge once: net_debt used in the DCF = A$306.8m (ex-lease) + A$312.2m (lease liabilities) = A$619.0m. This matches the company's own 'Total capital = net assets + net debt + lease liabilities' definition.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material minority interest -- Sims Metal, ANZ Metal and SLS are wholly owned; SA Recycling (SAR) is a 50% joint venture, equity-accounted (not consolidated), so SAR's economics enter the P&L as a non-cash 'share of profit of joint ventures' inside EBIT/EBITDA. Actual cash received from SAR is via dividends (A$56.7m FY25, A$80.6m FY24), not the accrual profit share. Because the component build is anchored to OCF-based FCF (OCF already reflects cash SAR dividends received, not SAR's equity-accounted profit), no separate SAR adjustment is applied to the FCF base; the gap between SAR's equity-accounted profit share and cash dividends received is absorbed as ordinary non-cash-working-capital-like noise inside the reported OCF-capex FCF history used to derive owner-FCF CAGRs. This is a modelling simplification, flagged here rather than silently assumed away.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF via the owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md route (cyclical, non-US industrial with material leases). Sims is a highly cyclical global metal-recycling and IT-asset-repurposing (SLS) business: statutory EBITDA margin has ranged from -0.7% (FY2020 COVID trough) to 10.5% (FY2022 commodity-price boom), averaging ~5.3% across FY2019/23/24/25. FY2026 full-year results (reported 2026-09-19, NOT YET in Metrics.csv -- the FY2026 annual PDF is not yet published/extracted) showed underlying EBIT +167.6% to A$468.0m on revenue A$8,007.5m (underlying EBITDA ~A$728m, ~9.1% margin), driven substantially by an exceptional (>1000% YoY) spike in DDR4 memory resale pricing in the SLS segment that management itself guides to soften materially in H1 FY2027 (SLS EBIT guided to just A$75-90m for H1 FY27 vs an implied H2 FY26 run-rate far above that). The stock fell ~13% on results day on this guidance despite the earnings beat. FOLLOWING THE CYCLICAL METHOD: base_revenue is anchored to the actual FY2026 revenue (verified qualitatively via the Analysis JSON's news of the 19-Sep-2026 results release, cited per the task brief as usable for setting assumptions even though not yet in the CSV), but the FY0 EBITDA MARGIN used for the DCF base case (6.2%) is a MID-CYCLE NORMALIZED margin -- well below FY2026's DDR4-inflated ~9.1% underlying margin, and above the FY2025 trough of 4.3% -- reflecting a structurally improved (SAR JV scale, larger/higher-margin SLS) but still-cyclical business once the DDR4 spike fades, consistent with management's own H1 FY27 guidance. Historical CAGRs and the last_fcf anchor use the CSV's verified OCF-capex FCF series (owner FCF = reported FCF, SBC immaterial at ~0.2% of revenue, no material interest income to strip -- SGM carries net debt, not net cash).

bear.narrative: The H1 FY27 guidance downgrade (SLS EBIT $75-90m) is the leading edge of a sharper DDR4 pricing/volume correction than management expects -- the >1000% YoY price spike fully reverses and repurposed-unit resale margins compress toward memory-commodity levels, taking SLS back near its pre-boom run-rate for several years while GPU repurposing remains unproven and stalls in certification. Simultaneously, record Chinese steel export volumes persist or worsen, keeping ANZ ferrous margins pinned near market floors and pressuring NAM/SAR export-exposed volumes; a global construction/manufacturing slowdown (the macro risk flagged in the Analysis JSON) further softens ferrous demand. Revenue contracts in year 1 before stabilizing at low growth; EBITDA margin stays close to the FY2025 trough (4.3-5.0%) rather than recovering to a higher mid-cycle level, and the Unimetals-style counterparty risk in portfolio-simplification divestments recurs at least once more.

base.narrative: Metal (NAM, ANZ) trading margins normalize to a mid-cycle level as Chinese ferrous export oversupply gradually eases and US EAF/tariff support persists; SA Recycling JV continues bolt-on M&A and scale gains; SLS settles into a structurally larger but more moderate growth phase once the DDR4 pricing spike fades per management's own H1 FY27 guidance, with GPU repurposing a longer-dated (12-24mo) option not yet in the base case. Revenue growth is low-single-digit (volume plus modest price), EBITDA margin ramps from 6.2% toward a 6.8% mid-cycle steady state -- above the FY19-25 historical average of ~5.3% (SAR/SLS mix improvement) but well below the FY2026 DDR4-inflated ~9.1% underlying margin. Cash tax rate ramps from a still-recovering ~15% to a normalized ~26% (AU statutory-adjacent, consistent with FY22/FY23 cash-tax-paid/EBIT ratios of ~22-24%). Working capital consumes cash on growth (trading-margin business carrying inventory/receivables net of payables), captured at -12% of the revenue increase.

bull.narrative: Non-ferrous (copper/aluminium) strength from AI-driven electrification persists longer than expected, US tariff protection holds NAM/SAR margins elevated, and Chinese steel export oversupply eases faster on new EAF capacity, lifting ANZ. SLS avoids the feared H1 FY27 DDR4 air-pocket -- data-centre refresh timing proves less lumpy than guided, GPU repurposing certification succeeds ahead of the 12-24mo guided window and becomes a second structural growth leg alongside memory. SAR JV bolt-on M&A continues compounding scale. EBITDA margin ramps to an 8.7% mid-cycle steady state, still below the FY2026 DDR4-spike peak but durably above history on the structurally larger, higher-margin SLS mix.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35, but bear weight is raised to 25% (bull correspondingly trimmed to 25%) because (a) this is a trading-margin commodity business with a demonstrated -0.7% to +10.5% EBITDA-margin range across just the last 6 fiscal years -- genuine two-sided cyclical risk, not a stable compounder with a fat left tail only -- and (b) the market's own -13% reaction to the FY26 beat on H1 FY27 SLS guidance shows the single largest current earnings driver (DDR4 resale pricing) is already flagged by management as unsustainable at FY26 levels, which is closer to a known near-term headwind than a symmetric unknown. The core Metal business also faces a named, currently-unresolved structural headwind (record Chinese steel export oversupply) with no management-guided resolution date.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
